title: Compatibility shim for embeddings & rerank: error normalization and pagination contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers using third-party embeddings/rerank clients and older Redwood SDKs expect deterministic pagination cursors, legacy error codes, and a consistent response shape. Recent runtime changes produced minor schema differences (cursor format, next_page semantics) and consolidated error surfaces which caused integration breakage for enterprise customers and partners.
goals: Provide a backward-compatible compatibility layer (shim) for embeddings and rerank endpoints so existing clients don't need immediate code changes.
Normalize error codes and messages to documented legacy values while retaining internal observability mapping.
Stabilize pagination semantics: canonical next_cursor format, deterministic page sizes, and clear behavior for empty result sets.
Deliver migration guidance and test vectors for customers and partner SDKs.
Create telemetry and health checks to detect compatibility regressions post-deploy.
non_goals: This ticket does not change model scoring or vector representations.
It does not implement new embedding or rerank algorithms — only surface compatibility fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Embeddings endpoint accepts legacy cursor tokens and returns next_cursor in the previous string-encoded format for requests with compatibility flag; verified with 1000-sample regression test.
Rerank endpoint returns identical response fields and ordering for the canonical test set used by partners (link in assets).
HTTP error codes map back to legacy set (400/401/403/404/409/429/500) with stable error.code and error.message fields documented in the migration guide.
Pagination behavior: page_size cap enforced, empty pages return next_cursor=null and items=[], and callers receive consistent Content-Range style metadata where previously documented.
No measurable latency regression (>3ms P50) for the endpoints in canary region compared to baseline.
deliverables: Compatibility shim implementation behind runtime flag
Migration guide and changelog entry for API consumers
End-to-end regression test suite (embeddings + rerank) and test vectors
Telemetry dashboards showing compatibility flag usage, error-normalization rates, and pagination anomalies
Rollout playbook: canary -> ramp -> rollback criteria
risks: Potential performance overhead from additional serialization/deserialization in shim; mitigation: optimize hot paths and benchmark.
Edge cases in cursor encoding between language SDKs causing hard-to-reproduce customer bugs.
Incorrect error mapping could surface sensitive internal messages; mitigation: strict allowlist for messages.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable compat-shim for 5% of traffic in region us-east-1; monitor latency and error normalization metrics.
Phase 2 (ramp): increase to 35% after 48 hours if no regressions; engage Partner Success to verify integrations.
Phase 3 (global): full rollout across hosted regions and flag default-on for Dedicated tenants opting in; publish migration guide.
Rollback: switch flag off globally and invalidate any ephemeral compatibility cursors issued in last 24 hours.
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor parsing/serialization across supported SDK encodings (utf-8, base64 variants).
Integration tests exercising page boundaries, empty result pages, and back-to-back pagination calls.
Contract tests validating legacy error.code and error.message values for a matrix of error conditions (auth, quota, rate limit, malformed request, backend failure).
Performance benchmarks comparing P50/P95 token latency with and without shim under representative load.
Partner smoke tests: coordinate with 3 top customers to validate their staging integrations.
notes: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after partner incident where a third-party client failed to iterate pages due to cursor format change.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Nguyen: Eng team prototyped a flag-based shim; initial microbench shows +1.8ms P50 overhead in lab.
2026-03-12 - PM sync: Decided to preserve legacy error.code values and add an internal mapping table rather than surface internal messages.
2026-03-13 - Design review: agreed on explicit next_cursor=null for terminal pages; UX will include Content-Range-like header for clarity.
2026-03-14 - Eng update: merged cursor parsing helpers and opened PR for canary rollout automation (PR #5892).
implementation_notes: Expose behavior behind a per-tenant feature flag 'compat.embeddings_rerank_v1' for Dedicated/private customers.
Add an API-level request parameter 'compat_mode=legacy' accepted by SDKs for explicit migration testing.
Instrument mapping metrics: count of normalized errors, count of legacy cursors accepted, and number of synthetic cursors issued by shim.
Keep a hardcoded allowlist of error message templates to avoid leaking internal diagnostic strings.
